notes: Account summary: Mid-market B2B SaaS (developer tools for observability). Product team evaluating Hosted API for fast rollout; goal is to migrate high-volume inference to Dedicated for cost predictability.
Trial recap (hosted API 14-day pilot): avg sustained QPS 2.3 across region, peak observed QPS 12 during support-batch run, steady-state concurrency ~35 across 2 service routes (chat + embeddings).

Token mix observed during trial: ~65% requests are short prompts (<128 prompt tokens) with short completions (~64 tokens); 35% are long generation flows (prompt ~200 tokens, completion ~600 tokens) used for summarization and knowledge extraction.

Latency targets: product team wants p95 < 220ms for interactive chat flows; allowed p99 up to 400ms for long summarize jobs. Current hosted p95 ~180ms for short paths, p99 spikes to 520ms on peak bursts (reason: cross-region routing + KV warmup).

Cost sensitivity: target blended cost reduction of 40-60% moving to Dedicated. Finance has pinned ARR budget band to $150k-$350k; procurement wants clear per-token and per-hour cost model and sizing worksheet.
Security: company requires SSO/SAML + audit logs; data residency must remain in us-east-1 for initial rollout. They requested KMS integration for encryption of model artifacts in Dedicated.
Quote from head of product: "We need a predictable monthly bill and failover plan — demo looked good but we need numbers for capacity sizing before exec sign-off."

POC technical notes: SE ran load ramp with synthetic traffic; peak concurrency during POC (simulated customer spike) = 280 concurrent requests over 90s window, average token output per second peaked at ~48k tokens/s across the cluster.

Redwood recommendation from demo: start Dedicated with a small reserved pool equivalent to 4 x A10G-class GPUs (or 2 x H100 if they prefer throughput headroom) with autoscale burst to 8 for sustained peak windows; enable prefix caching for chat routes to reduce effective token spend on repeated prompts.

Sizing / forecasting asks from FluxScale: a) map POC QPS/concurrency to Dedicated GPU count at expected 60/40 short/long token split, b) show per-hour cost and projected monthly token spend, c) fallback policy if pool saturated (route to hosted fallback).
Operational requirements called out: fine-grained rate limits per route, per-API-key token breakdown in Console, and 180-day audit log retention (enterprise add-on).
Open technical questions: network egress estimate for VPC peering; expected cold-start warmup for KV cache after model rollout; SAML attribute mapping for Azure AD (customer uses Azure).
Procurement path: they want sales pricing + draft SOW to review with legal by 2026-04-05. Finance expects TCO comparison spreadsheet vs continuing hosted spend.

Competitive notes: they evaluated OpenAI for simplicity but saw unpredictable cost at scale; Anthropic was benchmarked but latency on long generations worse in our testbed. Customer prefers Redwood's unified routing + Dedicated option.

Action items we own: deliver Dedicated capacity worksheet (Priya), draft SOW & pricing (Alex), run one more stress run with longer token-heavy jobs to validate throughput assumptions (customer/SE joint test on 2026-03-17).
